summary: REPAIR-REVIEW-02: Reviewed 83679d8..9643cd8 and directly affected source, SDK dependencies, contracts, and tests. Six remedy dispositions: file ownership partially corrected, with a clean-checkout regression; canonical POSIX paths and plan digest normalization accepted; explicit remote evidence requirements accepted; tree navigation and approval revocation accepted; retirement preserving work/history accepted; NUL-delimited committed-path parsing partially corrected, with whitespace corruption remaining. Stateful UTF-8 command decoding accepted. The exact-HEAD ship-check-02.log, stamped 2026-09-30T13:14:13.980Z, shows 48/48 tests passing and successful types, lint, prompt check, build, and final isolated Pi RPC verification. This review performed only source inspection and nonmutating probes, with no delegation, remote calls, builds, or effectful tests. No other review results were read. The documented destination-pinning blocker remains open; this candidate is not merge-ready. The user must choose the auto-merge release policy. Hosted CI attempt 2 remains billing-blocked before steps; live writer, interactive rendering, protected server merge, and macOS execution remain unconfirmed. Native profile metadata does not satisfy the formal custom-profile gate.

findings.detail: Documented release blocker remains: when a PR is retargeted after the destination checks but before the merge mutation, an unchanged head still satisfies --match-head-commit. The request contains no atomic approved-destination precondition, so it can merge into a different destination. Another client-side read cannot close this interval. Keep automatic merging release-blocked until the user selects a policy that resolves or disables this authority.
findings.evidence: Delivery.merge checks baseRefName/baseRefOid at lines 806-807, then separately invokes gh pr merge with only the expected head at line 820. The subsequent read checks only MERGED state. The pipeline retarget fixture changes the destination during protection lookup, before the final view; it does not exercise retargeting between that view and mutation.

findings.detail: The new ownership guard rejects legitimate clean files when Git converts their checkout representation. For example, with core.autocrlf=true or a text/eol=crlf attribute, git show returns the committed LF blob while fileHash reads CRLF working-file bytes. Their hashes differ before any external edit, so the first worker edit or rewrite fails with 'External change'. Compare against the clean checkout representation or recorded clean preimages while retaining the raw-byte recheck before writing.
findings.evidence: Lines 50-54 compare hash(git show HEAD:path) directly with the raw working-file hash. Read-only Git hash-object probes showed LF and CRLF content normalize to the same Git blob f41418672ee3d93b03124bf4a6753f23c179d0fc, while the actual hash helper produced different SHA-256 values. The new files regression uses an LF-only baseline and does not cover checkout conversion.

findings.detail: The NUL-delimited path stream still passes through Delivery.git, which trims stdout. If the first committed pathname starts with whitespace, that whitespace is removed before scope validation. An explicitly approved file such as ' leading.ts' therefore commits successfully and then falsely blocks as outside scope. Preserve raw stdout for NUL-delimited Git output.
findings.evidence: Delivery.git returns result.stdout.trim() at line 117; commit splits that result on NUL at line 479. A nonmutating probe through the actual helper transformed ' leading.ts\u0000' into ['leading.ts']; scopeAllows([' leading.ts'], original) was true and the parsed-path check was false. Existing regressions cover Unicode, backslashes, and an embedded newline, but no leading whitespace.
